DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 39 s. 2022 May 16, 2022 HON. JIMS C. FULLECIDO Vice-Mayor Maunicipality of Libungan, Province of Cotabato Dear Vice Mayor Fullecido. This has reference to your letter dated 24 January 2022 wherein you are seeking this Qepartment's legal opinion regarding the following issues: "1. Are the allowances like RATA and clothing under Personal Services for regular employees can be considered as current obligation chargeable against the reenacted budget? 2. Under the reenacted budget, what are the legal bases of the Local Chief Executive to withhold and control the funds specifically on the fuel expense under the Office of the Vice Mayor?" In reply to your as defined under Section 3060) of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), as amended, obligations refer to an amount committed to be paid by the local government unit for any lawful act made by an accountable officer for and in behalf of the local government unit concerned. Moreover, Section 3231 of the LGC provides that only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing position, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed re-enacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. Äccordingly, "statutory obligations", are those demandable obligations derived from an express provision of law, and "contractual obligations", those obligations incurred by virtue of contracts entered into by the local chief executive pursuant to Section 22(c) of the LGC, that were authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursements shall be in accordance SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. — In case the Sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. therewith. Relatedly, Section 306(k) of the LGC states that Personal Services refer to appropriations for the payment of salaries, wages and other compensation of permanent, temporary, contractual, and casual employees of the local government init. Consistently, under Local Budget Circular No. 1452 dated 02 March 2022, issued by the DBM, uniform/clothing allowances and representation and transportation allowances (RATA) falls under "other compensation", particularly authorized allowances/benefits. In view Of the foregoing, salaries, including other compensation, of those who have existing plantilla positions, under the category of Personal Services may be considered as current obligations chargeable against the reenacted budget. Notwithstanding to the foregoing, we also encourage you to seek the administrative expertise of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) on this particular issue. As to the second query, as previously discussed, the consequence in case the sanggunian fails to enact the annual appropriations is that the budget of the preceding year is reenacted. Note, however, that there shall be no new programs, projects and activities. In other words, what the law prohibits is the disbursement of funds not authorized in the annual/supplemental budget for the preceding year, and no ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In that regard, this Department opines that the Local Chief Executive cannot withhold nor control the funds under the reenacted budget if such item was part of the annual/supplemental budget for the preceding year. Notwithstanding, we would like to reiterate that the opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same, and is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse tary for Local Government OSEC/EMAJLLLS-LRALL copy furnished: DIR.
